description: Nothing behind the face — four slit eyes burning in black stone, wreathed in dark. Its attack is to fall on you.
lore: A face of black stone, four slit eyes lit orange down it, red marks cut above and below them, the whole thing hanging inside a wreath of slow dark that takes fire when it moves. It does not strike. It rises, and it comes down on you with everything it weighs, meaning to crush. And the eyes shut first — all four, a breath before the stone cracks — so whatever was doing the looking is gone before the breaking starts.

There are two accounts of it and neither has won. One: it is a shell the emptying made when it had nothing left to work with, the outside done beautifully, the inside not attempted. The other: it is one of the masks, left lying too long near [[lore/the_hole_under_the_mountain|the mouth]], and no longer an object. The crackers prefer the first. The second has a next question in it.

[[characters/cfe826c1|Jehanne]] was sent a rubbing of the red marks, on the reasoning that a priestess reads things. She kept it through a winter. In spring she burned it, and told the sender the marks say nothing at all — in the voice she keeps for the prayers she no longer believes. She has not gone east since.
gm_notes: The shell-or-mask argument stays unresolved on purpose; if it is ever settled, settle it toward the cave. The red marks have no assigned meaning in canon — Jehanne's burned rubbing is a leaf event, not a beat. Do not give the marks a reading.
